A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSPT research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original MSPT benchmark results, hyperparameter studies, memory/runtime measurements and baseline reproductions.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds patch-locality diagnostics and comparative training-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The PMSA equations, partitioning, pooling, transformer blocks and training objectives are retained. Appendix A.3 newly documents geometric descriptors and RoPE, but does not establish that the implemented procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six PDE benchmarks, ShapeNet-Car and AhmedML. The added locality and efficiency studies introduce no new physical prediction task or dataset; their mesh-size variations concern experimental settings.

E2.justification: v2 expands efficiency comparisons beyond the existing Transolver example to include GNOT, ONO, OFormer and Galerkin Transformer in Table 8. Table 6 also introduces random ordering as a locality comparator. Main accuracy-comparison memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols measure within-patch spatial dispersion against random ordering and training efficiency over varying mesh sizes. Table 8 specifies 1,000 iterations per epoch and matches MSPT's 32 patches to Transolver's 32 slices. Existing benchmark splits, objectives and training configurations are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supporting analyses: Appendix A.1 tests whether ball-tree traversal actually preserves patch locality across six PDE benchmarks, while A.7 compares memory/runtime scaling against multiple methods. These address partition quality and comparative scalability beyond the retained patch-count, pooling and error-map studies.

E5.justification: The new locality diagnostic introduces distribution summaries: median, p90, p99 and maximum dispersion across patches, plus a histogram. These describe spatial variability, not uncertainty across training runs. Neither version provides repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 6 and 8 add substantive locality and efficiency results. At 500,000 points with 32 patches/slices, Table 8 reports MSPT versus Transolver memory of 22.49 versus 34.94 GB, but training times of 797.75 versus 547.38 seconds per epoch. Main accuracy scores remain unchanged. Appendix C corrects MSPT's Darcy error from 0.76 to 0.63, in units of ×10−2, matching the existing main-table value.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces a mathematical definition of patch dispersion as mean squared distance from the patch centroid for the new locality diagnostic. Existing attention equations, complexity reasoning and benchmark metric definitions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about unified local/global attention, accuracy, arbitrary geometries and million-point scalability. Added supporting evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 interprets locality as predominantly spatially coherent with an outlier tail. New A.2 relates patch-count selection to physical interaction scales and limiting attention regimes. A.6 also explains compatibility with additional physics-informed regularizers while stating that reported experiments retain standard objectives.

D1.justification: v2 adds an MSPT code link, specifies coordinate/reference-grid descriptors and within-patch RoPE in A.3, and clarifies that Figure 5 timings include ball-tree construction, permutation and padding. These improve documentation; the existing training-configuration table is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and discussion covering PDE-Transformer, global-local point-cloud tokenization, PhyFlow, XPINNs and RoFormer; NeuralCFD is no longer cited. The central positioning relative to Transolver, UPT/AB-UPT and Erwin remains intact. Reference deduplication and publication updates are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely verbatim. Changes comprise limited related-work expansion, additional appendix explanations and subsections, acknowledgments, cross-reference updates, bibliographic cleanup and corrections such as CDF to CFD.

P2.justification: v2 adds the locality histogram and two tables, expands Figures 4–5 captions and reflows existing material. The original diagrams, plotted results and error-map images are retained. Appendix visualizations and reproduction tables are renumbered rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through direct locality diagnostics, broader efficiency evidence, implementation details and a code link, while correcting the inconsistent Darcy value. These are useful but limited gains because the main accuracy evidence remains unchanged. The new efficiency table also exposes slower training at matched 32 patches/slices, a tradeoff not fully reflected in the retained broad computational-cost claims.
